payload.name: Complete-enumeration-in-memory-extraction
payload.description: When a source message enumerates multiple distinct items (advice, preferences, attributes, goals), ensure all are captured in the extracted or merged memory, not just the first subset.
content: When processing a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct items (e.g., 'X, Y, and Z', bullet points, or 'also'), extract every item. Do not truncate the list based on perceived relevance or order.

Represent the full set either as separate memory candidates per item or as one candidate containing the complete enumeration; if merging with an existing memory, ensure the merged memory still contains all distinct items.

Before finalizing an ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, verify the candidate or resulting memory covers every distinct item present in the source evidence; if any item is missing, correct the candidate or issue the appropriate update.

solves: The failed diagnosis showed an extraction candidate dropping the last item of a three-part advice list, leaving memory incomplete and a reference claim missing. This Skill addresses the general mechanism of incomplete extraction from enumerated lists, applying whenever a message presents multiple distinct durable items that should all be stored. It does not apply when the enumeration is illustrative rather than exhaustive, or when the message explicitly prioritizes a single item.
